A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching methods, datasets and core experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original single-task and sequential fine-tuning experiments across three model families, including component comparisons, counting-bias probes and detailed benchmark results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds layer-subset ablations, efficiency measurements and quantitative and qualitative recovery analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same selective-tuning recipes, frozen components, next-token training loss and optional LwF objective. The new layer-subset experiments investigate ablation settings without revising the proposed SA Proj. and MLP Gate&Up methods.

E1.justification: The five target datasets, eight held-out benchmarks and LCS-558K captioning probes are retained. The added recovery analysis reuses the existing CUB200–PixmoCount–PathVQA sequence; it introduces no new dataset, domain or task requirement.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain LwF, LoRA, MoE and WiSE-FT alongside the component-tuning configurations. The efficiency table profiles already evaluated methods, while the new layer-subset conditions are ablations. Newly cited continual-learning methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Existing splits, prompts, training budgets and accuracy metrics remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce first-23 versus last-5-layer controls, stage-wise recovery probing and a throughput protocol processing 384 samples under common hardware and software conditions (Appendix E.3, E.5 and E.6).

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the analyses with a layer-freezing ablation, training-efficiency comparison and quantitative and qualitative tracking of forgetting followed by recovery (Appendix E.3 and E.5–E.7). These test additional questions beyond the retained composition experiments and residual-to-logit analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 newly specifies a Spearman correlation analysis across methods and checkpoints. The existing three-curriculum aggregation and paired t-tests remain unchanged; no additional seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates or confidence intervals are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 5 and all 24 detailed performance tables retain identical values. Substantial new findings include the layer-subset results, numeric-bias reversal during recovery, Spearman correlation of -0.84 with held-out performance, and throughput of 1.46, 1.27 and 0.44 samples/second for SA Proj., LoRA and MoE respectively. Figure 4 also removes one counting example.

T1.justification: The transformer equations, residual decomposition, training objectives, numeric-token-bias definition and appendix logit-delta calculations remain mathematically equivalent. Revised notation and expanded mechanistic explanations introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit claim to be the first systematic study of rehearsal-free sequential skill adaptation in LMMs with broad held-out monitoring and recoverable forgetting. The principal selective-tuning and output-distribution-shift claims otherwise retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the layer-subset results and newly hypothesizes that PathVQA introduces other token biases that prevent complete recovery (Appendix E.6). The limitations now emphasize massive/commercial models and billion-sample training, replacing discussion of longer sequences, alternative architectures and additional modalities.

D1.justification: The new efficiency experiment documents H100 memory capacity, DeepSpeed, bfloat16, 384 processed samples and absence of competing processes. Conversely, v1's explicit code URL is replaced by 'Code will be made available.' Existing training and dataset-processing details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wei et al. (2025) on intra/inter-modal forgetting and Zhao et al. (2025), MLLM-CL, and explains its positioning against architectural approaches and its baseline selection. Shenfeld et al. was already discussed in v1's appendix and is relocated into related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodological motivation and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Related-work paragraphs are reordered, detailed task descriptions move into Appendix A, the LLM-writing-assistance disclosure is removed, and affiliations and appendix organization change.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document-wide typography, text-block dimensions and running headers, with extensive relocation and resizing of retained displays. It adds Figures 11–13 and Table 6, and redesigns Figure 4 from four examples to three.

improvement.justification: The layer-freezing experiment and recovery probes provide more direct support for v1's proposed forgetting mechanism, while Table 6 adds useful evidence about computational costs. These strengthen the existing study without resolving its broader generalization limits. Removing the code URL weakens access information, but the added empirical support yields a modest net improvement.
